substeps.label: C3 · hot-mount, cut face down
substeps.caption: Hot-mount each piece with its cut face down, in conductive compound so the SEM doesn't charge. The walls stand up in the mould. Use a compound with good edge retention: the last layer's pools are at the very top edge of each wall.
substeps.watch_out: a rounded edge erases the last layer's pools, which sit at the very top of each wall.

substeps.label: C3 · 12 mounts
substeps.caption: Two mounts a part, 12 in all. Engrave square.part.piece on the back of each mount. The parts holding the repeated settings and the controls give the first look at scatter.

substeps.label: C4 · grind 1.5 mm to the centreline
substeps.caption: Grind away the 1.5 mm to the centreline on coarse paper. Measure the mount's height before and during, so you know when you're there; ±0.3 mm still cuts every wall near mid-length.
substeps.watch_out: overshoot and the plane moves off mid-length. Measure the mount's height as you go.

substeps.label: C4 · polish
substeps.caption: Then 320 and 800 grit, 3 µm diamond, and a 0.05 µm final polish. 316L is soft and can smear pores shut: on a few walls, re-polish and re-image to check the porosity doesn't change.
substeps.watch_out: 316L smears and can close pores over. Re-grind 2-3 mounts 0.3 mm deeper and image them again: that measures how much one section scatters.
